newsitem.title: USA: Interdigital appeals Motorola patent dispute.
newsitem.headline: Interdigital appeals Motorola patent dispute.

text.p: Interdigital Communications Corp told Reuters Tuesday the company is continuing the appeal process of a 1995 federal court decision favoring Motorola Inc in a patent dispute.
Interdigital's brief in support of its appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit in Washington, D.C. is due October 9, Interdigital spokeswoman Susan Sutton said.
In 1995, a jury of the U.S. District Court of Delaware ruled in Motorola's favor after a trial that combined competing lawsuits of the companies.

At issue was Interdigital's claim that Motorola products infringed Interdigital patents for TDMA or Time Delay Multiple Access technology. The jury agreed with Motorola's assertion that the patents were invalid and that its products did not infringe.

Interdigital failed in its efforts to have the verdict reversed or to obtain a new trial from the presiding judge, Chief Judge Joseph Longobardi. The Delaware records were officially closed August 26, court documents show.
